name: Web NFC
plain: Asks to read or write NFC tags with your phone.
meaning: Lets a page scan NDEF tags and write to them. Only while the page is visible and focused. Android Chrome only.

web.api: new NDEFReader(); reader.scan(); reader.write(); permission nfc

access.prompt_ui: Chrome Android prompt: Scan NFC tags; needs a gesture to write.

data.metric: NDEF records (url, text, mime, smart poster)

limits.headline: Can scan NFC tags or save to them with your phone, after you allow it
limits.user_action: You tap Scan tag or Save to tag, then hold your phone near it.
can: Scan an NFC tag when your phone touches it
Save text or a link onto a tag after a tap
Scan only while the page is open and in front
cannot: Work in the background or when you switch apps
Save onto a tag without a tap on the page
Use your phone's wallet or payment cards
Work on iPhone, desktop or most browsers other than Chrome on Android
limits.differs: Only Chrome on Android supports it. iPhone and other browsers do not.

story.what_it_is: A site asks to read or write NFC tags using your phone.

marketing.name: Web NFC
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say Web NFC lets sites read and write NFC tags on Android.

story.for_you: You tap your phone to a tag or card and the page reads it. It only works while the page is open and on screen, and only on Chrome for Android.
story.for_makers: Makers can build tag based tools without a native app: event check in, inventory, product info and smart posters.

use_cases.example: You tap an NFC tag at a hotel to check in on the hotel's website.
A tag on a shirt opens its product page with sizes.
Event staff scan NFC tickets with a phone browser to let people in.
A web based scavenger hunt reads tags hidden around a city.
A warehouse worker taps a tag on a shelf to update inventory.
A cloned tag could be used to trick a page that trusts what it reads.
